summary: Verified runtime crash fix for Layout.tsx useEffect. Injected init script patching window.scrollTo to return a Promise (reproducing the old bug trigger). Navigated all 7 routes via nav-link-* selectors + browser back. No error overlay, 0 console errors, 0 'destroy is not a function' errors. Smoke flow passed: load-demo -> analyze -> /results shows recommended-material-name ('Micro-Perforated Film'); PDF downloaded (PackIntel_Tomato_analysis-80.pdf); /history lists 80 runs and history-open-80 reopens the run successfully.
critical_code_review_comments: Layout.tsx useEffect now uses block body -> returns undefined -> React treats as no cleanup. Fix is correct.
Scanned src for expression-bodied useEffect arrows (useEffect(() => expr, ...)); none found. Drawer.tsx, MaterialsPage.tsx, HistoryPage.tsx all use block-body effects with proper cleanup/no-return.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Runtime crash 'destroy is not a function' fully resolved. Verified with patched scrollTo returning Promise. All nav routes and core analysis->results->history->PDF flow work without errors.
rca of the issue: Newer Chrome makes window.scrollTo return a Promise. Prior Layout.tsx had expression-bodied useEffect: useEffect(() => window.scrollTo(0,0), [pathname]) — its implicit return (the Promise) was treated by React as the cleanup destroy function, causing 'destroy is not a function' on re-run. Fix: converted to block-body effect so it returns undefined.
